name: Starter: Scottish Gaelic
about: Scottish Gaelic in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Gaelic order.

words.bi: be (tha: is, bha: was, bidh: will be)
words.a: that (after a question word); his, her; to
words.aig: at (agam: at me, agad: at you, aca: at them)
words.an: the (am before b, f, m and p); whether (a yes-or-no question)
words.ag: at (before a verb's noun: -ing; a' before a consonant)
words.do: your (to one person); past marker after cha or an
words.rach: go (chaidh: went, thèid: will go, deach after cha)
words.ann an: in (ann am before b, f, m and p)
words.is: be (is: is; bu: would be; is toil leam: I like)
words.toil: will, pleasure (is toil leam: I like)
words.air: on (orm: on me, ort: on you)
words.ma: if (mas e do thoil e: please)
words.fad: all through (fad an latha: all day)

mas-e-do-thoil-e.about: Literally if it's your will, to someone you call thu; mas e ur toil e to anyone else.

what-s-your-name.text: Dè an t-ainm a tha ort

the-check-please.text: An cunntas, mas e do thoil e

items.text: Halò! Cupa cofaidh, mas e do thoil e.
items.means: Hello! A cup of coffee, please.
wrong: Halò! Cofaidh cupa, mas e do thoil e.
Halò! Cupa cofaidh, mas do e thoil e.

items.text: Tì agus uisge, mas e do thoil e.
items.means: A tea and a water, please.
wrong: Tì agus uisge, mas do e thoil e.
Tì agus uisge, mas e thoil do e.

items.text: Cupa bainne, mas e do thoil e.
wrong: Bainne cupa, mas e do thoil e.
Cupa bainne, mas do e thoil e.

items.text: Halò! Tì, mas e do thoil e.
wrong: Halò! Tì, mas do e thoil e.
Halò! Tì, mas e thoil do e.

items.text: Tha mi gu math, tapadh leat.
wrong: Mi tha gu math, tapadh leat.
Tha gu math mi, tapadh leat.

items.text: Tha, mas e do thoil e.
wrong: Tha, mas do e thoil e.
Tha, mas e thoil do e.

items.text: Tha, tapadh leat. Mar sin leat!
wrong: Tha, leat tapadh. Mar sin leat!
Tha, tapadh leat. Mar leat sin!

items.text: Chan eil, tapadh leat. Mar sin leat!
wrong: Eil chan, tapadh leat. Mar sin leat!
Chan eil, tapadh leat. Mar leat sin!

items.text: Halò! Dè an t-ainm a tha ort?
wrong: Halò! Dè an t-ainm a ort tha?
Halò! Dè an t-ainm a tha mi?

items.text: Halò! Tha mi toilichte do choinneachadh.
wrong: Halò! Mi tha toilichte do choinneachadh.
Halò! Tha toilichte mi do choinneachadh.

items.text: Gabh mo leisgeul, càite a bheil am fòn?
items.means: Excuse me, where is the phone?
wrong: Gabh mo leisgeul, càite a tha am fòn?
Gabh mo leisgeul, càite a bheil an fòn?

items.text: Aon leabhar, mas e do thoil e.
wrong: Aon leabhraichean, mas e do thoil e.
Aon leabhar, mas do e thoil e.

items.text: Dà chupa cofaidh, mas e do thoil e.
wrong: Dà cupa cofaidh, mas e do thoil e.
Dà cofaidh chupa, mas e do thoil e.

items.text: Gabh mo leisgeul, dè a chosgas e?
items.means: Excuse me, how much is it?
wrong: Gabh mo leisgeul, dè a e chosgas?
Gabh mo leisgeul, dè chosgas a e?

items.text: Halò! An cunntas, mas e do thoil e.
wrong: Halò! Am cunntas, mas e do thoil e.
Halò! An cunntas, mas do e thoil e.

items.text: Tha mi a' bruidhinn beagan Gàidhlig.
items.means: I speak a little Scottish Gaelic.
wrong: Tha mi ag bruidhinn beagan Gàidhlig.
Tha mi bruidhinn a' beagan Gàidhlig.

items.text: Tha mi ag iarraidh uisge, mas e do thoil e.
wrong: Tha mi a' iarraidh uisge, mas e do thoil e.
Tha mi iarraidh ag uisge, mas e do thoil e.

items.text: Tha mi a' fuireach ann an taigh beag.
items.means: I live in a small house.
wrong: Tha mi ag fuireach ann an taigh beag.
Tha mi a' fuireach ann an beag taigh.

items.text: Tha mo mhàthair a' fuireach an seo.
wrong: Tha mo mhàthair ag fuireach an seo.
Tha mo mhàthair a' fuireach seo an.

items.means: There's a bathroom in the house.

items.text: Bidh mi a' dol dhan sgoil.
wrong: Bidh mi ag dol dhan sgoil.
Mi bidh a' dol dhan sgoil.

items.text: Gabh mo leisgeul, càite a bheil an stèisean?
items.means: Excuse me, where is the station?
wrong: Gabh mo leisgeul, càite a tha an stèisean?
Gabh mo leisgeul, càite a bheil am stèisean?

items.text: Bidh mo mhàthair a' dol dhan bhaile mhòr.
items.means: My mother goes to the city.
wrong: Bidh mo mhàthair ag dol dhan bhaile mhòr.
Bidh mo mhàthair a' dol dhan mhòr bhaile.

items.text: Tapadh leat. Feumaidh mi a dhol a-nis.
items.means: Thank you. I have to go now.
wrong: Tapadh leat. Feumaidh mi a dol a-nis.
Tapadh leat. Mi feumaidh a dhol a-nis.

items.text: Bidh mi a' dol dhan bhaile mhòr a-màireach.
items.means: Tomorrow I'm going to the city.
wrong: Bidh mi ag dol dhan bhaile mhòr a-màireach.
Bidh mi a' dol dhan mhòr bhaile a-màireach.

items.text: Chan urrainn dhomh a dhol an-diugh.
wrong: Chan urrainn dhomh a dol an-diugh.
Chan urrainn mi a dhol an-diugh.

items.text: Feumaidh mi a bhith ag obair a-màireach.
wrong: Feumaidh mi a bhith a' obair a-màireach.
Feumaidh mi a tha ag obair a-màireach.

items.means: I have a brother and a sister.

items.text: Tha mo bhràthair ag obair ann an Dùn Èideann.
wrong: Tha mo bràthair ag obair ann an Dùn Èideann.

items.text: Is toil le mo phiuthar ceòl.
Tha a màthair ag obair an-diugh.
wrong: Tha a mhàthair ag obair an-diugh.

items.text: Tha caileag bheag aig mo phiuthar.
items.means: My sister has a little girl.

items.text: Bu toil leam cupa tì, mas e do thoil e.
items.means: I'd like a cup of tea, please.
wrong: Bu toil mi cupa tì, mas e do thoil e.

items.means: I drank too much coffee today.

items.text: Tha an t-iasg seo glè mhath.
wrong: Tha an t-iasg seo glè math.

items.text: Bidh sinn ag ithe aig seachd uairean.
wrong: Bidh sinn ithe aig seachd uairean.

items.text: Thèid sinn air a' bhàta a-màireach.
items.means: We'll go on the boat tomorrow.
wrong: Chaidh sinn air a' bhàta a-màireach.

items.text: Bha mi ann an Leòdhas an-uiridh.
items.means: I was in Lewis last year.
wrong: Robh mi ann an Leòdhas an-uiridh.

items.text: Cha deach mi a dh'obair an-dè.
items.means: I didn't go to work yesterday.
wrong: Cha chaidh mi a dh'obair an-dè.

items.text: A bheil thu a' tighinn a-nochd?
wrong: A tha thu a' tighinn a-nochd?

items.text: Bha sinn a' coiseachd fad an latha.
wrong: Bha sinn coiseachd fad an latha.

items.text: Bu toil leam a dhol a Steòrnabhagh.
items.means: I'd like to go to Stornoway.
wrong: Bu toil mi a dhol a Steòrnabhagh.

concept.line: A plain Gaelic sentence starts with its verb, then who or what: Tha an cofaidh fuar (is the coffee cold).

tha says where someone or something is, or what they're like (Tha mi sgìth: am I tired), while is says who or what someone or something is, often as 'S e … a th' ann: 'S e tidsear a th' innte (it's a teacher that is in her).

words.means: nam = in my; nad = in your

concept.line: After mo (my), do (your), a meaning his, cha, the past marker do and some other words, many first consonants soften, written with an h: màthair → mo mhàthair (my mother), ceannaich → cha do cheannaich (not did buy).

words.means: agam = at me; agad = at you

concept.line: A bheil starts a present yes-or-no question (A bheil thu sgìth?: whether are you tired?), and a question word comes first (Càite a bheil an taigh-beag?: where that is the toilet?).

words.means: a' = in the act of; ag = in the act of

concept.line: aig, air and le join a pronoun: aig + mi is agam (at me), air + thu is ort (on you), le + mi is leam (with me).
mo (my) and do (your) soften the next word and go with family and the body (mo mhàthair: my mother); for most things Gaelic says the thing at you: an càr agam (the car at-me: my car).
